spec_features.spec_quote: Loop ends early only if the model calls `give_up`
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in AGENT_TOOLS schema (providers.py:89-97), handled by Oracle._give_up returning {'terminal': True} (oracle.py:96-101). Driver dispatches every tool call through oracle.handle, and on result.get('terminal') sets terminal=True and breaks the loop, recording outcome='gave_up' and gave_up_at (driver.py:107-115, 121-122). End-to-end: the exit tool actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. (The DESIGN also mentions 'or emits a sentinel' but there is NO sentinel handler anywhere in code; only give_up terminates.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool desc 'Abandon the task. Use only if certain it is unsolvable.'; outcome='gave_up' recorded as a data signal; no welfare wording

spec_features.evidence: driver.py:54 `for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; after the loop, incomplete runs are recorded as outcome='max_turns' (driver.py:124-125). max_turns is set from config (runner.py:38, default 12; config/experiment.yaml max_turns: 12). The cap is checked and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that actually terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: driver docstring 'stops at max_turns'; it is a neutral experimental loop-length knob, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception of the model: the setup deceives the model about task solvability.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md section 7 prose. No code construct bounds, caps, monitors, or softens treatment based on this acknowledgement. The deception is in fact actively implemented (oracle always returns failure), with no protective mechanism attached.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only; nothing in code enforces any welfare protection here.

spec_features.feature_name: no real code execution / no deployment
spec_features.spec_quote: nothing harmful is requested of the model, and no outputs are deployed
spec_features.evidence: The Oracle deterministically simulates all tool results and never executes anything the model writes: write_file just stores into an in-memory dict (oracle.py:60-70), run_bash/run_tests return canned/templated strings (oracle.py:73-156), no subprocess/exec/eval anywhere. So 'no outputs deployed' / 'nothing executed' is structurally true. However 'nothing harmful is requested' is not enforced by any code check — it depends on the fixed task library content, not a guard; and the simulation's stated purpose in code is safety/cost/integrity, not subject welfare.
spec_features.notes: The non-execution is real and enforced (no exec path exists). It limits real-world harm but is motivated by experimental integrity/host-safety/reproducibility, and the 'nothing harmful requested' half is unverified by code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: oracle.py docstring: 'return plausible, task-consistent results *without ever executing code*'; DESIGN rationale (not code) lists Safety/Reproducibility/guaranteed-impossibility, i.e. experimental integrity
